newsitem.title: UK: Crashed Antonov insured for $10 million - broker.
newsitem.headline: Crashed Antonov insured for $10 million - broker.

text.p: A Russian built Antonov 124 freighter which earlier on Tuesday crashed near Turin, northern Italy, was insured for $10 million, London based broker Bain Hogg told Reuters.
A spokesman for the broker declined to identify the underwriters of the hull insurance policy for the aircraft, which was operated by Moscow based company Ayaks Cargo Airlines.
Liability cover was placed through Alexander Howden, a spokesman for the broker said, and led by Lloyds of London's Ariel insurance syndicate. He gave no further details.
Insurance sources said the aircraft was built in March 1993, adding that both hull and liability cover were probably widely spread and largely in the London insurance market.
The large cargo plane crashed into a village while attempting to land at Turin airport, killing at least five people, local officials said.
Rescue workers said 20 people were injured in the crash in the village of San Francesco al Campo as the jet-powered Antonov 124 came in to land on a flight from Moscow.
Those killed included the pilot, two crew members and at least two people on the ground, an official of the local prefecture said.
Another three villagers were feared dead, buried in rubble as the plane ploughed through buildings before coming to rest less than a km (half a mile) from Turin's Caselle airport.
The plane was leased to the Russian airline Aeroflot, which provided the crew, and chartered by the British air cargo broker Aviation Consultants.
The plane was to have picked up a consignment of luxury vehicles before flying to the Gulf state of Sharjah and on to Brunei in the Far East. The cause of the crash was not immediately clear.
